text:
maria: Heads-up — telemetry shows a bunch of recent requests routed to canary at ~50% even though Console shows the canary split at 10% :grimacing:
alex: saw that too. are these from dedicated infra or hosted?
sanjay: looks like a runtime-config push went out earlier — an API client set rollout_override=50. Deploy bot also rolled a change at 1763001200.
deploy-bot: deploy finished: service/runtime-config v1.12.4 by @sanjay at 1763001200 :white_check_mark:
yuki: wait, who is allowed to push runtime-config overrides? product assumed console is the single source of truth for traffic splits.
alex: historically we had two sources: Console (persisted policy) and runtime API (ephemeral overrides). No clear precedence documented. runtime overrides win at decision time in the router right now.
maria: that's the problem — many customers look at Console and get surprised. we need clear ownership and UI cues.
sanjay: technical reason: runtime API needs to support emergency quick rollbacks and region-level overrides, so it takes precedence. but we can add guard checks.
yuki: product perspective: console should be the default control plane. overrides must be explicit and visible (who did it, why, expiry).
alex: agreed. suggestion: 1) show "effective split" + source in Console UI, 2) expose override metadata in the API & logs, 3) set a TTL on runtime overrides unless marked persistent.
maria: +1. also we should make the precedence rules explicit in the docs and in the SDKs.
sanjay: implementation detail: router currently picks the highest-priority source where value!=null. quick pseudo:
```text
# precedence order (current)
if runtime_override: use runtime_override
elif console_policy: use console_policy
else: fallback_default
```
We could change to require a signed "allow_override" flag in the console policy to permit runtime overrides.
yuki: that would keep console ownership by default and allow emergency ops when a policy grants permission.
alex: we should also add an audit field on each route decision: {source, actor, ts, ttl}. that will make debugging easier.
maria: action items: - draft RFC for "override gating" and UI + logs - quick patch to add effective-source in Console for next week - telemetry query to find how many active runtime_overrides exist now
sanjay: i'll open the RFC and do a first-pass patch for router audit metadata.
yuki: i'll update product doc and run it by legal for compliance notes.
alex: i'll add the dashboard widget card to show active overrides and their owners.
maria: thanks everyone. can we set a temporary policy: all runtime overrides must include a TTL <= 1h unless an admin explicitly marks persistent?
sanjay: agreed, i'll enforce TTL if missing in runtime-config handler.
yuki: :thumbsup:
maria: filing a follow-up in #eng-releases for rollout when ready.
